web.title: Ghanti Pakdo: Christmas Kitty Party Bell Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Ghanti Pakdo is a fast listening and reflex kitty party game with a bell. Rules, a sample Christmas story with trap words, scoring, twists and FAQ for 8 to 20 ladies.
web.intro: Ghanti Pakdo is a seated reflex game for a kitty party: ladies sit in groups of four around a stool with a bell on it, the host reads a made-up Christmas story, and the moment she says "ghanti" the first lady to lift the bell scores a point. The first lady to reach 5 points wins her group and plays the final. The crazy twist is the trap words: the host slips in sound-alikes like "ganthi", "Shanti" and "Santa ki gaadi", and anyone who moves her hands on a fake word loses a point. It needs only a bell, a stool and chairs, so it fits any December or Christmas kitty.
materials: One small bell per group of 4 (a puja ghanti, a cycle bell or a steel glass with a spoon inside)
One stool or small table per group
A short story written by the host, using "ghanti" about 5 times and trap words about 8 times
Paper and pen to keep score
A small prize for the winner
steps: Split the ladies into groups of 4. Each group places 4 chairs in a small circle around a stool, with the chairs a little apart so no one bumps heads.
Put one bell in the centre of each stool.
Every lady sits with both hands flat on her knees. She may not stand up or lean off her chair during the game.

The host reads her Christmas kitty story aloud, slowly at first. Example: "Christmas wali kitty thi. Shanti aunty ne ganthi wala dupatta pehna. Tabhi darwaze ki ghanti baji, aur Santa ki gaadi ruki..."
Whenever the host says the word "ghanti", the first lady in each group to lift her group's bell gets 1 point. She puts the bell back and everyone returns her hands to her knees.
When the host says a trap word such as "ganthi", "Shanti", "ghanta", "Santa" or "kanthi", anyone who lifts her hands off her knees loses 1 point.
A scorer in each group keeps the points. The first lady to reach 5 points wins the group.
Group winners meet in a final around one stool, played with their eyes closed. The first to 3 points wins the prize.
rules: Hands stay on your knees until you hear the real word "ghanti".
Standing up, pushing or grabbing another lady's hand cancels your point.
Moving on a trap word costs 1 point.
Lifting your hands too early, before the host finishes the word, also costs 1 point.
First to 5 points wins the group; first to 3 in the final wins the game.
variations: Eyes-closed final: the bell is placed in the centre and finalists must find it by touch after the host says "ghanti".
Santa rule: whenever the host says "Santa", everyone must raise both hands, and the last lady to do it loses a point.
Change speed: the host reads slowly, then very fast, then in a whisper, so ladies have to listen hard.
tips: Write the story before the kitty so the real word and the trap words are spaced out and surprise everyone.
Keep chairs an arm's length apart and the stool low, so ladies reach with their hands, not their heads.
A soft cloth bag or a steel glass works if you have no bell; the game is about who touches it first.
Ladies who are waiting can be scorers and judges, which keeps them involved.
Play one practice round so everyone hears what the trap words sound like.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Ghanti Pakdo?
faq.a: It works best for 8 to 20 ladies split into groups of 4. All groups play at the same time while the host reads one story.

faq.q: What do you need to play Ghanti Pakdo?
faq.a: One bell, one stool and four chairs per group, a short story written by the host, and paper to keep score. A steel glass can replace the bell.

faq.q: What are good trap words for Ghanti Pakdo?
faq.a: Use words that sound like ghanti: ganthi, Shanti, ghanta, kanthi, Santa ki gaadi and chhatri. Mix 8 trap words with about 5 real ones.

faq.q: Is Ghanti Pakdo a good game for a Christmas kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. The host's story can be about Santa, jingle bells and a Christmas kitty, it takes 10 to 15 minutes and needs no decoration or cooking.

faq.q: Is Ghanti Pakdo safe for older ladies?
faq.a: Yes. Everyone stays seated, only hands move, and chairs are kept apart, so no one has to run or bend down.
